World map — nine art styles, three exploration states

Same geography throughout: Haven lower-left with three roads, the lake north-centre, the impassable mountain wall east, forest NW, burned frontier NE, delta SE, dry hills SW. Each style's three states are derived from its own full map, so terrain is identical across a row. Click any image to enlarge.

Round 2 — built from your reference images

E — Middle-earth

Your Tolkien reference. Amber parchment, pure black pen-and-ink, mountains as clusters of inked peaks, coastlines with fringing contour lines, hand-lettered names, compass rose and scale bar.

Fog = undrawn parchment. The ink simply stops where the survey stopped.

your reference

F — Cork + under-lighting

Your cork map. Laser-cut cork raised off a dark stained panel, engraved detail, warm amber LED glow leaking out from beneath every coastline.

Fog = bare unlit panel. The world is physically built and lit as you explore — the strongest progression of anything here.

your reference

G — Torn adventurer's chart

Your second hand-drawn reference. Teal watercolour sea, brown-grey ink relief, tiny ships, dashed routes, big compass rose, burnt and water-stained torn edges.

Fog = the sheet is missing. You recover the map in fragments; mid-game is scraps you've pieced together.

your reference

H — Illustrated atlas

Your Aredia reference. Satellite-like terrain in muted greens and tan, slate-blue ocean, tiny white settlement dots, small pale serif labels, thin border frame.

Fog = cloud deck. Note it picked up our real region names — Haven, Lake Ashenmere, Thornwood Reach, The Ashmark, Gravel Downs, The Fallow Coast.

your reference

I — Painted collector map

Your Malo reference. Lavishly painted biomes with individual trees and rock, teal sea with swirling currents, ribbon-banner place names, ornate silver compass.

Fog = painted cloud banks. Richest of the nine, and the busiest.

your reference
Round 1 — the earlier four, for comparison

A — Realistic

Satellite-and-relief rendering, low afternoon sun.

Fog = volumetric cloud. Landmarks are scenery, not icons.

B — Hand-drawn (round 1)

Aged parchment, iron-gall ink, watercolour wash, sea serpent.

Fog = undrawn parchment. Superseded by E, which is the same idea done better.

C — Very cartoony

Bold outlines, chunky shapes, candy palette.

Fog = storybook cloud. Highest icon readability.

D — Embroidered tapestry

Dyed wool on linen; satin-stitch rivers, french-knot forests.

Fog = bare unwoven cloth, with faint guide-lines that read as rumour.
